title: Deployment choice decision grid - sales lab (WIP)
body:
Purpose:
Quick, tactical decision grid and speaker notes for SDRs/AE technical calls — help field pick the right deployment story (Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private) based on buyer signals. Not a full playbook, more of a lightweight one-pager + call script fragments.

Audience:
- Technical buyers (platform/infra teams) evaluating inference at scale
- Product/AI teams worried about latency/cost/regulatory controls
- GTM (AE/SE/SDR) prepping for discovery and early technical qualification

How to use:
- Start with buyer signals checklist (left column) during discovery call
- Use the decision grid to land on a recommended deployment story
- Pick 2–3 talking bullets from the recommended box for the demo/technical dive
- Capture objections and next-step play (trial, security review, sizing worksheet)

Buyer signals checklist (quick):
- Data residency/regulatory requirement: yes/no
- Peak QPS and request size distribution (small conversational vs long doc synth): low/medium/high
- SLA/uptime mandate (legal/finance-backed): yes/no
- Budget visibility: pay-as-you-go vs committed/monthly?
- Team capability: in-house infra + ops vs prefers managed service?
- Security controls needed: KMS/HSM, private networking, audit logs?
- Model customization necessity: fine-tune vs prompt engineering?

Decision grid (guidance, not hard rules):
- Hosted API (recommended if):
  * No strict residency or heavy compliance requirement
  * Moderate throughput or bursty usage where quick time-to-value matters
  * Team prefers minimal ops; wants SDKs + streaming + rapid prototyping
  * Budget is flexible (usage-based) or early-stage evaluation
  Talking bullets:
  - "Fastest path to production: API and SDKs take minutes to integrate; streaming and function calls supported."
  - "We manage the runtime, autoscaling, and model versioning — you get consistent performance without ops overhead."
  - "Built-in observability per-route/token-level costs so you can tune spend quickly."
  Typical next steps:
  - Sign up for hosted trial, attach sample traffic, set up token/cost guardrails
  - Provide example prompt sets for our Optimize recommendations

- Dedicated (recommended if):
  * Predictable, sustained throughput and cost sensitivity; you want reserved GPU pools
  * Need for isolation between workloads without full private control plane
  * Want SLA-backed latency/uptime guarantees for customer-facing products
  Talking bullets:
  - "Reserved capacity gives predictable unit economics and consistent tail latency."
  - "Configurable autoscaling and burst lanes for spiky traffic while keeping cost predictability."
  - "You can pin model versions and run canary rollouts within the same console."
  Typical next steps:
  - Capacity sizing session + pricing estimate (we use the throughput template in GTM kit)
  - Technical deep-dive with infra/ops to review networking and data isolation behaviors

- Private deployment (recommended if):
  * Data residency, regulatory compliance, or air-gapped/strict governance required
  * Customer operates VPC/on-prem and demands CMK/KMS integration, audit logs, and control plane placement
  * Enterprise procurement preferred (license + support) over usage billing
  Talking bullets:
  - "Private control plane that can be deployed into your VPC or air-gapped environment — keys and audit logs under your control."
  - "On-prem option supports restricted networks and integrates with customer KMS/HSM for encryption at rest/rotation."
  - "We provide migration tooling and runbook templates to speed up onboarding while maintaining compliance constraints."
  Typical next steps:
  - Security questionnaire and architecture alignment (SOC/ISO details in appendix)
  - Enterprise contract discussion and delivery timeline (4–12 weeks depending on infra)

Objection handling snippets (short):
- "We can’t trust a hosted vendor with our PII" -> "If PII regulation applies, our Private deployment option keeps data and keys in your control; we also offer SOC/ISO artifacts and dedicated support for evidence collection."
- "We need sub-100ms tail latency" -> "Tail latency depends on model size + sequence patterns; Dedicated with reserved pools and optimized kernels gives far lower variance than best-effort shared services — we can run latency benchmarks with your workload profile."
- "We already run inference in-house" -> "Our differentiator is the serving runtime and ops: batching, KV cache, and routing policies that lower per-token cost and simplify rollouts; many customers migrated to reduce ops overhead and improve unit economics."

Call structure (5–6 minute sequence for rapid qualification):
1) 60s intro + context-setting (who uses the model, 1–2 KPIs)
2) 120s buyer signals checklist (capture the items above)
3) 90s recommendation (pick Hosted/Dedicated/Private + why)
4) 60s next steps and CTA (trial, security pack, capacity workshop)

Example one-liners for AEs/SDRs:
- "If you need a fast POC with low ops, try Hosted — we can get a sample integration going this week."
- "If you expect steady, high throughput and want predictable cost, Dedicated is where teams lock in capacity."
- "If regs or audits mandate control of keys and network, Private is what we usually deploy for those accounts."

Appendix (metrics/benchmarks to pull into deck depending on audience):
- Latency (p50/p95/p99) examples for common models on Dedicated vs Hosted (internal perf table id: perf/latency-2025-q2)
- Unit cost delta: hosted per-token vs dedicated reserved capacity calculations (example sheet id: costs/dedicated-vs-hosted-2025)
- Compliance artifacts: SOC2 Type II, ISO27001 summary, private deployment checklist (links to Confluence)

Unresolved questions / TODOs (notes to self):
- Add concrete benchmark numbers for p99 tail on medium-sized models (ask SRE for latest run)
- Create a short slide with the migration timeline (hosted -> dedicated -> private) and typical gating items
- Confirm legal-friendly phrasing for "private control plane" to avoid overpromising

Quick checklist for pre-call prep (SE/AE):
- Load the account’s Security pack into notebook and review red flags
- Bring capacity worksheet and 3 sample pricing scenarios
- Prepare an anecdote of a similar customer migration (2–3 line summary)
- Share a follow-up template email that includes trial access + security artifacts

Version history:
- 2025-11-02 initial sketch by EB
- 2025-11-08 added objection snippets and call structure (Marcus)
- 2025-11-14 appended appendix items and TODOs (Asha)

Notes to self (styling / slides):
- Keep slide deck to 6 slides for discovery + decision: 1) problem + signals, 2) grid, 3) hosted bullets, 4) dedicated bullets, 5) private bullets + timeline, 6) appendix links & next steps.
- Avoid heavy technical diagrams on first call — they confuse; surface architectural details in follow-up SRE deep-dive.

End of sketch.

Contact: eleanor.briggs@redwood.ai (for feedback / additions)
